newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - CompUSA under pressure.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - CompUSA under pressure.

text.p: -- Salomon Brothers analyst David Childe made some cautionary comments on CompUSA Inc, according to a market source.
-- Childe said he expected CompUSA stock to be under pressure due to worsening conditions in the computer retail industry.
-- shares sank 6-1/4, or nearly 11 percent, to 51-1/8.

-- In a research report, Childe said CompUSA's retail computer sales -- which comprise 60 percent of its business -- "have decelerated to 0 percent from an estimated three to four percent in its September quarter, despite easier comparisons."
-- in the research report, Childe said "industry softness, promotions and CompUSA's current inventory position are some negative issues that are now surrounding the company."
-- said "industry sources have informed us that CompUSA has been canceling some desktop CPU orders, and that the stores appear to be modestly overinventoried at this point."
-- said company "has been very careful not to get mired in the industry's highly expensive 0 percent, 12-month financing and free printer-monitor promotions over the last year."
-- said if it becomes necessary to clear inventory, promotions "will ultimately have to be mirrored by CompUSA to some degree."
-- "There has been a distinct softening in overall retail computer sales over the past few weeks," Childe said.

-- said "best guess" is company will report earnings of $0.30 per share for the first quarter, ended in June, versus Wall Street consensus estimate $0.26-$0.27. CompUSA expected to report on Wednesday.
